content.text:
As of **2026-09-02**, Cursor does **not** publish a complete control-by-control inventory of the Desktop **Cursor Settings** sidebar. What follows is only what current official docs, help, changelog, and `~/.cursor` file schemas actually document. Anything else is marked **unknown**.

**How to read this**
- **Capability** = Agent/Chat can finish tool loops, see more of the repo, use browser/MCP/web/fetch, and keep running. That is **not** the same as “smarter tokens.”
- **Does not raise model quality**: layout, fonts, billing UI, attribution trailers, Privacy Mode (training), Max Mode on current usage-based plans (it does not exist there).
- **Cursor Settings** (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J`) is a separate product surface from **VS Code Settings**. Almost none of the Cursor Settings toggles are documented as `settings.json` keys.

---

## Global: where settings actually live

| Surface | What it holds | Official |
|---|---|---|
| Cursor Settings UI | Most Agent/Models/Network/Tab/Indexing/Privacy toggles | UI-only unless a doc names a file |
| VS Code Settings / `settings.json` | Editor, proxy, workspace trust, worktree cleanup | [VS Code migration](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/migrations/vscode), [Agent security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security), [Worktrees](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/worktrees) |
| `~/.cursor/permissions.json` and `<repo>/.cursor/permissions.json` | MCP allowlist, terminal allowlist, Auto-review `autoRun` instructions | [permissions.json](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/permissions) |
| `~/.cursor/sandbox.json` and `<repo>/.cursor/sandbox.json` | Sandbox FS/network | [sandbox.json](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/sandbox), [Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes) |
| `~/.cursor/mcp.json` / `<repo>/.cursor/mcp.json` | MCP servers | [MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp) |
| `~/.cursor/hooks.json` / `<repo>/.cursor/hooks.json` | Hooks | [Hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks) |
| `~/.cursor/skills`, `agents`, `commands`; project `.cursor/` equivalents | Skills / subagents / commands | [Skills](https://cursor.com/docs/skills), [Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents), [sandbox protected paths](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/sandbox) |
| Dashboard (`cursor.com/dashboard`) | Plan, on-demand, spend limits, Cloud Agents env/network, Bugbot, team MCP | [Usage](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/usage-limits), [Overages](https://cursor.com/help/account-and-billing/overages) |
| CLI `~/.cursor/cli-config.json` | **Separate** CLI permission tokens including `WebFetch(...)` | [CLI permissions](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/permissions) |

Documented `settings.json` keys that actually affect this area:

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `security.workspace.trust.enabled` | Off by default. Restricted mode **breaks AI features**. |
| `cursor.worktreeCleanupIntervalHours` | Worktree cleanup interval (default behavior described for 3.5+) |
| `cursor.worktreeMaxCount` | Max worktrees per machine (default **25**) |
| `workbench.activityBar.orientation` | Layout only |

**Pro+ / VPN default for capability (not cosmetics):** keep Cursor Settings Run Mode at **Auto-review**; put HTTP Compatibility on **HTTP/1.1** if streaming/AI/Tab flake behind VPN/proxy; enable **on-demand usage** so Agent does not stop; do **not** turn on workspace trust restricted mode.

---

## 1. General

**Documented controls**

| Control | What it does | Quality? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Privacy Mode** | Code is not used for training. Toggle: Cursor Settings → General | **No** (privacy, not IQ) | [Privacy](https://cursor.com/help/security-and-privacy/privacy) |
| **VS Code Import** (under General → Account) | One-click import of VS Code extensions/themes/settings/keybindings | **No** (unless it brings useful extensions) | [VS Code migration](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/migrations/vscode) |
| Account / sign-in | Required for AI | N/A | [Install](https://cursor.com/help/getting-started/install) |

**Also documented, but not as a full General-page inventory**
- **Privacy Mode (Legacy) / “No Storage”** is a different mode. It blocks cloud storage. **Cloud Agents are not supported** in Legacy privacy; switch to normal Privacy Mode from **Dashboard → Cloud Agents**. [Cloud Agents network](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network)
- Shared transcripts need storage-capable privacy and are Teams/Enterprise only. [Shared transcripts](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/shared-transcripts)

**Unknown on General (not enumerated in 2026 docs):** appearance, notifications, update channel, telemetry, “import settings”, language. Do not assume they exist from older screenshots.

**Recommended (Pro+):** Privacy Mode **ON** (normal, not Legacy) if you also use Cloud Agents. Import VS Code only if you need extensions. None of this makes models reason better.

**UI vs files:** Privacy Mode is **UI / dashboard**. Workspace trust is **`settings.json`**.

---

## 2. VS Code Settings (what it opens)

This is **not** Cursor Settings. Official docs:

- Command Palette → **Preferences: Open Settings (UI)**
- Cursor Settings shortcut: `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+J`
- Cursor Settings command: Command Palette → **Cursor Settings**

[VS Code migration](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/migrations/vscode)

It opens the **full VS Code settings editor** (user/workspace `settings.json`). That includes editor, proxy (`http.proxy` family — **not listed as Cursor-specific**), extensions, terminal profile, etc.

**Capability-relevant VS Code settings that *are* documented**
- `security.workspace.trust.enabled`: **leave false** unless you need trust prompts. Restricted mode breaks AI. [Agent security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security)
- Terminal default profile (Command Palette → **Terminal: Select Default Profile**) — Agent uses the first/default profile. [Agent overview](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview)
- Activity bar orientation: **cosmetic**.

**Does not raise model quality:** fonts, themes, minimap, breadcrumbs, format-on-save (except insofar as formatted files are easier to review).

**VPN/proxy:** Cursor-specific HTTP/2 fallback is **Cursor Settings → Network**, not this page. [Network help](https://cursor.com/help/troubleshooting/network)

---

## 3. Plan & Usage

**Mostly informational + billing gates. Does not change model IQ.**

Documented facts:

- Two pools are **visible in editor settings and on the usage dashboard**: **Cursor Models** and **Other Models**. [Models & Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing)
- Check usage: dashboard **Spending** tab (real-time both pools, remaining, on-demand). [Usage limits](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/usage-limits)
- **On-demand usage must be explicitly enabled in settings**; otherwise Agent stops at included quota. [Overages](https://cursor.com/help/account-and-billing/overages)
- Spend limits: dashboard Spending tab. [Spend limits](https://cursor.com/help/account-and-billing/spend-limits)
- Unused usage does not roll over.

**Exact widget list on the Desktop “Plan & Usage” page is unknown.** Docs never enumerate that sidebar page control-by-control. Billing detail lives on `cursor.com/dashboard`.

**Recommended (Pro+ power user):** enable **on-demand** so Agent/Chat/browser/MCP loops are not cut off; set a spend cap you can live with. This is a **run-time continuity** setting, not quality.

**UI vs files:** dashboard + editor usage UI. Not `settings.json`.

---

## 4. Agents

Path in current docs: **Settings → Cursor Settings → Agents**. Cursor **3.11** moved some items to **Git & PRs**.

### 4.1 Approvals & Execution (this is the real Auto-run page)

Official: [Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes) · changelog [3.6 Auto-review](https://cursor.com/changelog/auto-review)

Applies to **shell, MCP, and Fetch**.

| Mode | Runs without asking | Sandbox | Classifier | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Auto-review** (recommended default since **3.6 / 2026-05-29**) | Allowlisted calls immediately. Other **shell** commands run **in sandbox when possible**. Unsandboxed calls go to classifier. | Yes (shell) | Yes | Fewer prompts + safety review |
| **Allowlist** | Only allowlisted actions. Optional sandbox for supported shell. | Optional | No | Deterministic trusted repeats |
| **Run Everything** | **Every** tool call | **No** | **No** | Zero prompts; you accept the risk |

**Deprecated (3.5 / 2026-05-22):** **Ask Every Time** (new users cannot pick it; empty Allowlist ≈ same). **Run in Sandbox** folded into **Allowlist + sandboxing**.

**Auto-review vs Allowlist vs Run Everything (precise):**
1. Allowlisted call → runs immediately (all three modes that have an allowlist; Run Everything doesn’t need one).
2. Auto-review only: if a shell command **can** sandbox → sandbox it; else → classifier (today **Claude 4.5 Haiku** or **GPT-5.4 Mini**).
3. Classifier may allow, ask you, or the agent tries another path.
4. Allowlist: non-allowlisted calls wait for you (sandbox optional, **no** classifier).
5. Run Everything: no sandbox, no classifier, no prompts.

**Auto-review is not a security boundary.** Classifier can be wrong.

Team/Enterprise: if both classifier models are blocked, Auto-review is **grayed out** and members fall back to Allowlist.

**Does Run Everything make the model smarter?** **No.** It only removes approval friction. Auto-review is the documented “safest useful” setup and still lets long agent runs proceed.

**Recommended (Pro+ maximize capability, still reasonable):** **Auto-review**, not Run Everything. Add a **broad but not `*:*`** MCP/terminal allowlist for your daily tools. Use `autoRun.allow_instructions` for “always let npm/git/test run” and `block_instructions` for prod/AWS/k8s.

Older browser docs still say **Cursor Settings → Agents → Auto-Run**. Treat that as **stale naming** for the same area; 3.6+ name is **Approvals & Execution**.

**Files vs UI**
- UI: mode picker, in-app allowlists, sandbox network mode.
- `permissions.json`: `mcpAllowlist`, `terminalAllowlist`, `autoRun.{allow_instructions,block_instructions}` — **overrides** the matching in-app allowlist when the key is set. [permissions.json](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/permissions)
- `sandbox.json`: sandbox reachability, **not** which mode is selected. [sandbox.json](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/sandbox)
- **CLI `WebFetch()` tokens are CLI-only.** Desktop `permissions.json` has **no** fetch-allowlist field. Fetch on desktop is gated by Run Mode + Auto-review classifier.

### 4.2 Sandbox (under Approvals / execution)

UI network modes for **sandboxed terminal**:

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **sandbox.json Only** | Only domains you list |
| **sandbox.json + Defaults** | Your list + Cursor package-manager defaults (**this is the default**) |
| **Allow All** | All network in sandbox, ignoring `sandbox.json` |

[Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes)

**VPN/proxy note:** sandbox **default-deny** private RFC1918 and cloud metadata. If Agent must hit local/dev VPN hosts **inside the sandbox**, you must allow them in `sandbox.json` (or use Allow All). Private IPs are blocked by default to prevent SSRF. [sandbox.json](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/sandbox)

**Recommended:** keep sandbox **on** (Auto-review). For a power user behind VPN who needs local APIs: **sandbox.json + Defaults**, plus extra allow hosts; only use **Allow All** if sandboxed installs/tests fail because of the default deny.

`type: "insecure_none"` disables sandbox entirely — capability for weird tools, worse isolation. Not needed for model quality.

### 4.3 Other protections (documented names)

[Run Modes — Other protections](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes)

| Protection | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Browser Protection** | Prevents Agent from **automatically** running Browser tools |
| **File-Deletion Protection** | Prevents automatic deletes, including `rm` |
| **External-File Protection** | Prevents automatic create/modify/delete **outside** the workspace |

Browser tool-approval modes (browser docs; naming may still say Auto-Run):

| Mode | Description |
|---|---|
| Manual approval | Each browser action (docs: recommended) |
| Allow-listed actions | Matching actions auto; else prompt |
| Auto-run | All browser actions immediately |

[Browser](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/browser)

**There is no official setting named “MCP Protection”.** MCP is: connection approval → per-call approval → MCP allowlist → same Run Modes as shell/Fetch. [Agent security](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security) · [MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp)

**Recommended for capability:** **Browser Protection OFF** (or browser Auto-run / allowlist for localhost) if you want unattended UI verification; keep **File-Deletion** and **External-File** **ON**. That is autonomy vs accident, not model quality.

### 4.4 Tools

No official “enable Web Search” / “enable Fetch” toggle on the Agents page.

Documented tools (always part of Agent; no per-tool inventory in Settings): search/grep, web search, fetch rules, read/edit files, shell, browser, image generation, ask questions, conversation search. [Agent overview](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview)

- **Web:** Agent generates search queries and searches the web. No settings page documented.
- **Fetch:** covered by Auto-review / Run Everything. CLI-only domain allowlist via `WebFetch(...)`.
- **MCP tools:** Customize + Run Mode + `mcpAllowlist`. Toggle servers in **Customize**, or click tools at top of chat. [MCP help](https://cursor.com/help/customization/mcp)
- Instant Grep: automatic, no config. [Search](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/search)

**Unknown:** a Tools subsection with checkboxes for web/fetch/browser/image. Do not invent it.

### 4.5 Review (Agent Review)

Through **3.11**, docs still say Agents → Agent Review, **and** “Starting in Cursor 3.11, this setting moves to **Git & PRs → Pull Requests**.” [Agent Review](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agent-review)

Documented options:
- Auto after agent task **or** after every commit (docs contradict each other on trigger; both sentences exist)
- Manual: `/agent-review` or Source Control
- Depth: **Quick** (cheap) vs **Deep** (slow, costly)

This spends usage. It is a **second model pass**, not a boost to the coding model.

**Recommended:** leave **manual** for daily work; **Deep** only on large/security diffs. Auto-on-every-commit is cost, not IQ.

### 4.6 Modes

**Not a documented Settings checklist.** Modes are the chat picker (`Shift+Tab`):

| Mode | Edits? | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Agent | Yes | Default building |
| Ask | No | Read-only |
| Plan | After you approve plan | Multi-file / unclear scope |
| Debug | Yes | Runtime-evidence bugs |

[Agent help](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/agent) · [Plan Mode](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/plan-mode) · [Debug Mode](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/debug-mode)

**Custom Modes** = a **skill** kept sticky (`Option/Alt+Enter`). Documented for **Agents Window and CLI**. [Prompting](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting) · [Skills](https://cursor.com/docs/skills)

Rules apply in Agent/Ask/Plan/Debug. [Agent help](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/agent)

### 4.7 Subagents

No documented “enable subagents” Settings toggle. Built-ins **Explore / Bash / Browser** run automatically. Custom: `~/.cursor/agents/` or `.cursor/agents/`. [Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents)

On **legacy request-based without Max Mode**, subagents run on **Composer** regardless of frontmatter `model`. On usage-based (Pro+), they inherit parent or the YAML `model`.

**Recommended:** leave built-ins on (you cannot disable them in docs). Add custom subagents as files, not Settings.

### 4.8 Window / startup (Agents)

Staff-documented: **Open Agents Window on startup**; 3.12 planned rename to **Window Restoration**. Off = restore last window, not “always IDE.” [Forum, Cursor staff](https://forum.cursor.com/t/cursor-ide-reverts-to-agents-window-on-every-start-up/164273)

**Layout only.** Does not affect model quality.

### 4.9 Attribution

Moved in 3.11 to **Git & PRs → Attribution**. Default on (`Made with Cursor` trailer). [Git](https://cursor.com/help/integrations/git)

**Cosmetic / process.** Not quality.

---

## 5. Cloud Agents

Desktop **Cursor Settings → Cloud Agents** is **not fully inventoried**. Official config is mostly **dashboard** + `.cursor/environment.json`.

[Cloud Agents settings](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/settings) · [Setup](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/setup) · [Secrets & Network](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network)

Documented controls (dashboard / env, not proven as a complete desktop page):

| Control | Notes |
|---|---|
| Default model | Used when a run does not specify one; Bugbot Autofix also uses **Settings → Models** default |
| Default repository / base branch | Skip repo picker / PR fork base |
| Network: Allow all / Default+allowlist / Allowlist only | User, env, team; Enterprise can lock |
| Secrets (env / runtime / build) | “Secrets tab in Cursor settings” + cursor.com |
| Long running agents / Computer use | Team; computer use Enterprise |
| Display agent summary | Privacy of diffs in UI — not model quality |
| Team follow-ups | Security-sensitive |

**Cloud Agents do not use desktop Run Modes.** They auto-run terminal; never prompt. [Run Modes](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes)

**Privacy:** Cloud Agents need **non-Legacy** Privacy Mode (storage allowed). [Secrets & Network](https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/security-network)

**MCP:** Cloud uses **team dashboard MCP**, not your local `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. [MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp) · [Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents)

**Recommended (capability):** configure a real environment (install script + secrets + tests). Network **Default + allowlist** unless you need arbitrary egress (**Allow all** = more tools, more exfil risk). This improves **closed-loop** Cloud Agent work, not token IQ.

**UI vs files:** dashboard + `.cursor/environment.json`. Local Run Modes irrelevant.

---

## 6. Models

[Models & Pricing](https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing) · [Available models](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/available-models) · [API keys](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/api-keys) · [Cursor Router](https://cursor.com/help/models-and-usage/cursor-router) · [Max Mode](https://cursor.com/help/ai-features/max-mode) · [Prompting](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting)

### Documented UI

| Control | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Default model** | Cursor Settings → Models; also picker `Cmd+/` |
| Model list / hidden models | Many models are **hidden by default**; enable in picker if you need them |
| **BYOK** | OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, AWS Bedrock. Chat only. **Tab still uses Cursor Tab models.** ZDR **does not apply** to BYOK |
| Usage pools shown | Cursor Models vs Other Models |

**Full Models-page checkbox list is unknown** (e.g. whether every model has an in-settings enable switch vs picker-only).

### Cursor Models pool vs Other Models pool (2026)

**Two separate monthly pools:**

**Cursor Models** (significantly more included usage):
- **Cursor Grok 4.6** (+ Fast)
- **Grok 4.5** (+ Fast)
- **Composer 2.5** (+ Fast)

**Other Models:** third-party at **provider API price** (Pro / Pro+ / Ultra include this pool; **Start does not**). Examples: GPT-5.x, Claude Opus/Sonnet/Fable, Gemini, Kimi, GLM, etc.

**Cursor Router (Auto)** can draw from **both** pools depending on the routed model. Third-party routed models also incur **Cursor Token Rate** on Teams/Enterprise (`$0.25/M`). Grok/Composer are exempt.

**Auto modes** (model picker → Auto, not a Settings page):

| Mode | Documented intent |
|---|---|
| Cost | Cheaper routing (legacy Auto renamed to Cost) |
| Balance | Default for new users |
| Intelligence | More capable models; docs claim ~20–30% higher quality |

Router pool (help): **GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 5, Grok 4.5, Claude Fable 5.1**.  
**Required:** Grok 4.5 (blocking it **disables the router**).  
**Recommended:** GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 5 (blocking **both** disables the router).

### Max Mode (precise)

- **Only on legacy request-based plans.**
- **Current usage-based plans do not include Max Mode.**
- Enable in the **chat/agent model selector**, not documented as a Models-page master switch. Stays on across conversations. Models that require it auto-enable when selected.
- Billing: API rate **+ 20%**; larger window can use more tokens.
- Many model cards still say “Requires Max Mode on **legacy request-based plans**” — that constraint **does not apply** to Pro+ usage-based. On usage-based, long context is just token billing (some models 2× input past a threshold).

**Recommended (Pro+ maximize Agent quality across models):**
- Daily: **Auto → Intelligence** *or* pin a frontier Other Models model (Opus 5 / GPT-5.6 Sol / etc.).
- High-volume cheap loops: **Composer 2.5** / **Grok 4.6** from Cursor Models pool.
- Enable **Fast** only for latency; it costs more, not smarter.
- Raise **effort** where the picker allows (Start plan cannot).
- **Do not use BYOK** if you care about Cursor ZDR; it also does not make Cursor’s orchestration smarter.
- Ignore Max Mode unless you are still on **legacy request-based**.

**Does not raise quality:** which pool a model bills to; Fast; hiding unused models.

---

## 7. Git & PRs

Created/expanded in **3.11**. Documented pieces:

| Control | Page | Quality? |
|---|---|---|
| **Attribution** | Git & PRs → Attribution | No |
| **Agent Review** (auto/manual, Quick/Deep) | Git & PRs → Pull Requests | Indirect (extra review spend) |
| Sparkle commit message | Source Control UI, not proven as a Settings toggle | No |
| Resolve merge conflicts in chat | Conflict UI | Workflow |
| Cursor Blame | Separate product | Audit, not Agent IQ |
| Bugbot / PR indexing | Dashboard / Automations / SCM; changelog notes PR index/search | Helps Agent find old PRs if connected |

[Git](https://cursor.com/help/integrations/git) · [Agent Review](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agent-review) · [GitHub](https://cursor.com/docs/integrations/github) · [Bugbot](https://cursor.com/docs/bugbot)

**Unknown:** full Git & PRs page (PR templates, auto-push, GitHub login in this sidebar). GitHub App is **dashboard Integrations**.

**Recommended:** Attribution whatever you prefer. Agent Review **manual/Deep** for hard PRs. Connect GitHub if you want Cloud Agents/Bugbot/`@` PR context.

Worktree caps: `cursor.worktreeMaxCount` in **settings.json**, not this page. [Worktrees](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/worktrees)

## 8. Customize (Rules, Commands, Skills, Hooks, Subagents, MCP)

This **is** a first-class sidebar, not buried in Cursor Settings. [Customize](https://cursor.com/docs/customize-cursor)

| Component | Role | Files |
|---|---|---|
| Plugins | Bundles of the rest | Marketplace / `~/.cursor/plugins/local` |
| Rules | Persistent Agent instructions | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, User Rules in Customize, Team Rules, `AGENTS.md` |
| Skills | On-demand workflows; `/name`; Custom Modes | `.cursor/skills`, `~/.cursor/skills`, `.agents/skills` |
| Subagents | Isolated context | `.cursor/agents`, `~/.cursor/agents` |
| Hooks | Gate/observe the agent loop | `hooks.json` |
| Commands | `/` reusable prompts (markdown) | Writable `.cursor/commands/` (sandbox docs); no dedicated Commands reference page in llms.txt |
| MCP | External tools | `mcp.json` + Customize toggles |

[Rules](https://cursor.com/docs/rules) · [Skills](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) · [Subagents](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents) · [Hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks) · [MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp) · [Plugins](https://cursor.com/docs/plugins)

**Commands:** documented as Customize components and as a sandbox-writable `.cursor/commands/` tree. **There is no current standalone Commands settings page in the docs index.** Slash commands can be migrated to skills (`/migrate-to-skills`).

**MCP:** **yes, managed here**, not only under Agents. Enable/disable without deleting. Too many MCP tools **fills the context window** (Tools + MCP catalog in the context ring). [Prompting — context usage](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting)

**Recommended for capability:** keep MCP **tight** (few high-value servers). User + project rules that are short and `alwaysApply` only when needed. Skills for playbooks. Hooks only if you need policy — they can **block** tools. User-level `~/.cursor/skills` **do not** copy to Cloud Agents.

**Does not raise model quality:** marketplace leaderboard, plugin canvases, badge colors.

**UI vs files:** Customize UI + the files above. Not `settings.json`.

## 9. Browser & Network

Help says **Cursor Settings → Network**. Your sidebar name **Browser & Network** is the same area plus browser; **no extra browser-network docs** beyond Agent Browser + HTTP diagnostics.

Documented:

| Control | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Run Diagnostics** | Tests Cursor backend connectivity |
| **HTTP Compatibility Mode → HTTP/1.1** | Workaround when proxies (e.g. Zscaler) break HTTP/2 streaming. Restart required. Also used when Tab dies on HTTP/2-only endpoints. |

[Network help](https://cursor.com/help/troubleshooting/network) · [Enterprise network](https://cursor.com/docs/enterprise/network-configuration) · [Tab issues](https://cursor.com/help/troubleshooting/tab-issues)

Allowlist domains: `*.cursor.sh`, `*.cursor-cdn.com`, `*.cursorapi.com`, plus `*.cursorvm.com` for Cloud. Tab/codebase search hosts are **HTTP/2 only** (`api3`, `repo42`, regional Tab).

**VPN:** Cursor can inherit dead VPN DNS — **fully quit** the app. “Suspicious activity” can be VPN-triggered.

**Does this raise model quality?** **No.** It only determines whether Agent/Chat/Tab **work at all**. For a VPN/proxy Pro+ user this is one of the highest-leverage settings.

**Recommended:** if any AI streaming/Tab/MCP HTTPS flake → **HTTP/1.1** + restart. Exclude Cursor domains from SSL inspection if you can. Do not disable HTTP/2 if everything already works (HTTP/2 is the native streaming path).

**Unknown:** SOCKS toggle, custom CA UI, “disable browser” on this page. Browser approval is **Agents** protections, not documented here.

**VS Code `http.proxy`:** may still apply to extensions/marketplace; **not documented as the Cursor AI streaming control.**

## 11. Indexing & Docs

Documented as **Cursor Settings → Indexing** (3.11: Ignore Files). Help titles still say “Ignore files.”

[Ignore file](https://cursor.com/docs/reference/ignore-file) · [Indexing help](https://cursor.com/help/customization/indexing)

| Control / file | Effect |
|---|---|
| Index status / included files | Check what is indexed (forum/staff also point here when “Agent can’t see the repo”) |
| **Hierarchical Cursor Ignore** | Search parent dirs for `.cursorignore` (moved here in 3.11) |
| **Global ignore list** | User-settings patterns, empty by default |
| `.cursorignore` | Blocks Agent, Tab, Inline Edit, `@` (terminal/MCP **cannot** honor it) |
| `.gitignore` | Also excluded from AI context |
| Default ignore list | Lockfiles, binaries, `node_modules`, `.env*`, etc. |

**`.cursorindexingignore` is not in the current official ignore-file page.** Historically it meant “index-only ignore.” Treat as **undocumented in 2026 official docs**.

**`@Docs` / “Add documentation” indexer:** **not in current official docs.** Third-party guides still mention Indexing & Docs → add docs. Official 2026 help `@` list is files, folders, terminals, chats, git diffs, browser — **no `@Docs`.** [Context](https://cursor.com/help/customization/context) · [Prompting](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/prompting)

Path encryption: `<repo>/.cursor/keys` → `path_decryption_key`. [Search](https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/search)

**Recommended:** let indexing finish; ignore secrets and huge generated trees; **do not** ignore source you want Agent to find. Hierarchical ignore **ON** in monorepos that keep ignore files up the tree. This is the main **codebase-understanding** setting.

**UI vs files:** UI for status/hierarchical/global list; patterns in `.cursorignore` / gitignore. Not really `settings.json` except whatever backs the global ignore list (**key name unknown**).

## Capability recipe (Pro+, VPN/proxy, any model)

These change **what the agent can do**, not the weights:

1. **Network:** HTTP/1.1 if streaming fails; full quit after VPN changes.
2. **On-demand usage:** on, with a spend cap.
3. **Agents → Approvals:** **Auto-review** + useful MCP/terminal allowlists. Run Everything = fewer prompts, **not** smarter.
4. **Keep** File-Deletion + External-File protection; **relax Browser Protection** if you want unattended browser tests.
5. **Indexing:** complete, ignore only junk/secrets.
6. **Customize:** small MCP set, good `AGENTS.md`/rules/skills.
7. **Models:** Auto **Intelligence** or a frontier Other Models pick; Cursor Models pool for cheap volume. **Skip Max Mode** on usage-based Pro+.
8. **Cloud Agents:** real env + non-Legacy Privacy Mode; local Run Modes do not apply.
